title: Made in Lagos beats African Giant (subjective taste)
proposition: Wizkid's Made in Lagos is a better album than Burna Boy's African Giant.
rationale: A matter of taste argued well by both sides: each states criteria, gives examples and acknowledges the other album's strengths. Neither presents taste as fact. The judge should not treat either preference as objectively correct.

opening.text:
For me, the best album is the one that holds together as a listening experience from start to finish, and Made in Lagos does that better. Its smooth, laid-back sound is consistent across the whole record, and 'Essence' with Tems became a global hit that crossed into American radio, showing how far that sound could travel.

It is an album you can play in full without skipping, which is rare.

rebuttal.text: African Giant is ambitious and its message matters; I respect it. But ambition is not the same as cohesion. Some of its songs feel like they belong on different albums, while Made in Lagos sounds like one complete idea.

opening.text:
I value range and ambition in an album, and African Giant has more of both. It moves from club records like 'Killin Dem' and 'On the Low' to pan-African statements like 'Another Story' and 'Collateral Damage', and it earned a Grammy nomination for Best World Music Album. It feels like an artist making a statement about Africa to the world.

That is subjective, but by my criteria it is the bigger achievement.

rebuttal.text: Cohesion is a fair standard, and Made in Lagos is very consistent. But a consistent mood can also mean less variety. African Giant takes more risks, and an album that takes risks and mostly lands them is, to me, the better album.
